title: Hazratbal Crisis and Communal Tensions in East Pakistan
subtitle: The Hazratbal relic theft and communal violence in East Pakistan, 1963–1964
summary: On 27 December 1963, a relic believed by devotees to be a hair of the Prophet Muhammad was reported missing from the Hazratbal shrine in Srinagar. The theft prompted protests. On 3 January 1964, communal violence broke out in Khulna and nearby areas of East Pakistan; contemporary United Nations reporting recorded killings, arson, looting and destruction of property. Responsibility and the scale of violence should be described through attributed accounts rather than generalized blame.
heroTagline: From the Hazratbal relic theft to violence in East Pakistan
whyItMatters: The crisis shows how a religiously charged event in Kashmir became entangled with communal tensions and minority insecurity in East Pakistan. The United Nations record describes violence beginning in Khulna on 3 January 1964, while later scholarship treats the relic episode as a catalyst within broader regional dynamics. Casualty figures vary and are omitted here.
